text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty auto-page fired -> service: prod-edge-lb-health (P1). Incident PD-123456. Trigger: TLS handshake failures + target unhealthy across eu-west-1 edges. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-123456

miguel (oncall): acked PD-123456 :hand:

carla (netops): looking at ELB health + cert rollout logs. early signal from cdn-rotator job around 02:18 UTC.

ben (sre): seeing TLS errors spike in metrics: tls_handshake_failures 6.9% over 5m in eu-west-1. LB target health flapping for backend pool B.

ben (sre): curl from eu-west tester -> edge returns TLS handshake failure
```
$ curl -v https://edge-eu.example.com/health
* Connected to edge-eu.example.com (34.200.11.22) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: SSL: error in SSL library, (SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake failed
```

carla (netops): running aws elbv2 describe-target-health -> some targets in target-group tg-prod-backend-b show Unhealthy (502)
```
$ aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg-prod-backend-b
{"TargetHealthDescriptions": [{"Target": {"Id": "10.12.5.21"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Description": "502 from target"}}]}
```

eve (support): alerting ops-contacts for key enterprise customers in eu-west. preliminary count: ~3% of requests saw 5xx during the spike window. no large-scale page yet from customers but increased error rates on ingested logs.

dave (pagerduty): PD auto-escalation kicked to escalation policy "oncall-sre-rapid" at 02:22 UTC. miguel, if you want me to re-route to carla's team let me know.

miguel (oncall): keep oncall-sre first, carla please coordinate with infra to pause rotation if it's the rotator job. If it's cert chain issue, rollback immediate.

carla (netops): confirmed rotator job for cert rotation started @ 02:17 UTC with batch target pool B -> certs applied had new chain + SNI set to alt-hostname by mistake in template. rolling back cert to previous chain on pool B now.

ben (sre): coordinating failover: increasing weight on pool-A by 30% to drain pool-B while rollback proceeds. executing route weight change:
```
# internal cli
infra route-weight set --edge-pool pool-a --weight +30 --dry-run=false
```

ben (sre): weights updated. observing client traffic shift. healthchecks for targets backing pool-B still show 502s though.

carla (netops): rollback complete for pool-B certs (reapplied cert chain v2026-01-18). restarting edge proxy on affected hosts (edge-eu-4/5).

ben (sre): post-rollback: TLS handshake errors dropped to 0.6% in 2m, target health for 10.12.5.21 -> healthy.

miguel (oncall): nice. keeping PD open until stabilized for 15m. can someone confirm customer impact windows?

eve (support): estimate: impact window ~02:18-02:34 UTC (~16m). peaked at ~7% error rate for eu-west requests. affected customers: small subset of API keys hitting eu-west; no global outage. raising notices to customer success for affected enterprise accounts.

dave (pagerduty): PD status updated: acknowledged -> investigating. escalation paused.

carla (netops): quick root cause note: cert rotation job used template that set SNI alias to alt-hostname for pools referencing older TLS config; chain was correct but SNI mismatch made backend reject handshake. fix: validate SNI template on rotator and add preflight handshake check.

ben (sre): added temporary guard: rotator will run a dry-run handshake check against a canary host before applying to pool. patch submitted: https://git.internal/redwood/cert-rotator/pull/482

miguel (oncall): monitoring for 30m, if error rate <0.5% for 30m we can resolve. assigning postmortem to ben.

eve (support): customers notified. CS will follow up with impacted customers and include mitigation steps and timeline.

ben (sre): will draft postmortem, timeline + RCA + action items (fix rotator, add preflight, improve PD runbook for cert rotations).

miguel (oncall): closing notes: good quick ack, keep convo in thread. if anyone sees regressions ping PD channel.

incident-bot: PD-123456 status -> resolved (manual close) at 03:05 UTC. incident duration: ~47m (auto-page->close).

carla (netops): reaction :thumbsup: — follow-up runbook entry created in infra runbooks/docs/cert-rotation.md

ben (sre): postmortem owner: ben, due in 3 business days. assigned -> #pm-7892.

miguel (oncall): thanks all.
